about.source: LegiScan Connecticut bulk datasets, JSON variant, session_ids 2018, 2117, 2174, 2244
about.cohort_rule: House members whose service covers all four sessions, so tenure is held constant. Weir served exactly these.

definitions.filed: Member holds a primary-sponsor slot (sponsor_type_id 1) on a bill. Connecticut committee bills put the committee in that slot, so this counts member-introduced bills only. Resolutions (bill_type JR and R) are excluded.
definitions.first: Filed bills on which the member is the first-listed primary sponsor.
definitions.alone: Filed bills on which the member is the only sponsor.
definitions.hearing: Filed bills scheduled for a public hearing.
definitions.reported: Filed bills reported out of committee.
definitions.floor: Filed bills receiving a floor vote in either chamber.
definitions.cospon: Bills the member signed that another slot leads.
definitions.cospon_law: Of those, the ones that became law. Context only: raw cosponsorship rewards signing many bills and is not a measure of legislative work.

roster_cohorts.source: Committee ranking-member and freshman-class rosters are not in the LegiScan bulk datasets. They were assembled from the Secretary of the State's Register and Manual, CGA Bulletin No. 68 (2023-04-13), CT News Junkie committee-leadership reports, and election records. The rosters themselves are embedded below under `rosters`. The freshman class was then verified against the 2021 and 2022 LegiScan datasets.
roster_cohorts.note: Ranking posts changed hands between terms, so those cohorts are computed per term rather than over all four sessions. Weir held the Labor ranking post only in 2025-26; Tim Ackert (HD-008) held it in 2023-24.
roster_cohorts.still_open: Two 2023-24 ranking posts (Planning and Development, Veterans' Affairs) could not be established and are absent from that term's cohort of 23.
